Dear Ms. Reese:

          Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America LLC (“Natural”) hereby submits for
filing, pursuant to Section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act and Subpart A of Part 157 of the
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“Commission”) regulations, an abbreviated
application for a certificate of public convenience and necessity authorizing Natural to
construct and operate a new compressor station on Natural’s Amarillo system in Moore
County, Texas, and a new delivery point in Deaf Smith County, Texas. The Project will
allow Natural to provide 550,000 dekatherms per day of firm southbound transportation
service from various existing receipt points located in Natural’s Mid-Continent Zone to a
new delivery point located in Natural’s Permian Zone. Natural estimates the cost of the
Project to be $139 million.

       The Project will create 321,200 Dth/day of incremental firm southbound
transportation capacity on Natural’s Amarillo System which, when combined with 228,800
Dth/day of reserved unsubscribed capacity, will allow Natural to meet its contractual
obligations to provide 550,000 Dth/day of firm transportation service to the Project
Shipper.

       Pursuant to Section 7(c) of the Natural Gas Act (“NGA”),1 as amended, and in

accordance with Part 157 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“Commission”

or “FERC”) regulations,2 Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America LLC (“Natural”)

hereby files this abbreviated application requesting issuance of a certificate of public

convenience and necessity for authorization to construct, operate, and maintain the

Amarillo Expansion Project (“AMEX” or the “Project”).           The Project involves the

construction and operation of a new compressor station on Natural’s Amarillo System.

Specifically, Natural proposes to construct and install four (4) new gas-fired compressor

units with related Section 2.55(a) auxiliary facilities at a new compressor station in Moore

County, Texas, and a new delivery point to be located in Deaf Smith County, Texas (as

more specifically defined herein as “Project Facilities”).

       By utilizing existing unsubscribed capacity that Natural has reserved for the Project

and the capacity created by the Project Facilities, Natural will be able to provide 550,000

dekatherms per day (“Dth/day”) of firm southbound transportation capacity on Natural’s

existing Amarillo System. This capacity will be used to provide 550,000 Dth/day of firm

transportation service to IP Roman III Gas, LLC (“Project Shipper”). The Project Shipper

        To ensure timely construction of the Project, Natural respectfully requests that the

Commission issue an order approving the Project on or before August 1, 2027. The

issuance of the requested authorizations by that date will allow Natural to complete the

materials procurement and construction of the Project in a time frame compatible with a

        In support of this application and pursuant to the Commission’s regulations and

Rules of Practice and Procedure, Natural respectfully states as follows:

                                  I.      EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

        Natural seeks NGA Section 7(c) authorization for the Project to increase the

southbound firm transportation capacity of its Amarillo System by constructing a new

compressor station on property owned by Natural that was formerly used for a

compressor station known as Compressor Station (CS) 112.3 The proposed new

compressor station will be referred to as CS 112. The Project allows Natural to combine

existing unsubscribed capacity on its system with capacity created by the Project

       The Project is fully supported by a PA for a 10-year firm transportation service

agreement for 550,000 Dth/day with the Project Shipper. By using existing unsubscribed

available capacity, Natural is able to reduce the size of the Project Facilities that it needs

to construct to meet the natural gas transportation needs of the Project Shipper. The

Project will create 321,200 Dth/day of incremental firm southbound transportation

capacity on Natural’s Amarillo System which, when combined with 228,800 Dth/day of

reserved unsubscribed capacity, will allow Natural to meet its contractual obligations to

the Project Shipper. The Project Shipper’s capacity will extend from certain existing

receipt points located in Natural’s Midcontinent Receipt Zone to a new delivery point in

Natural’s Permian Delivery Zone to be located in Deaf Smith County, Texas (“Project

Path”).

       As more fully described in Section VI, Natural proposes to construct and operate

1) a new compressor station (referred to herein as “CS 112”) with four (4) compressor

units, each rated at 5,500 horsepower (Hp), providing a total of 22,000 Hp, 2) auxiliary

facilities located in Moore County, Texas, and 3) a new delivery point to be located in

Deaf Smith County, Texas. The proposed compression equipment will be constructed

within the boundaries of the abandoned compressor station site.

       The cost of the Project is approximately $139 million, as detailed in the attached

Exhibit K, Cost of Facilities.

       As discussed in Section VII below, Natural is also seeking pre-approval of certain

potentially non-conforming contract provisions included in the firm transportation service

        As discussed in Section VIII below, Natural proposes to use its existing reservation

transportation service to be provided on the Project Facilities. Given that the revenues

generated by the Project will exceed the cost of service associated with the Project,

Natural is requesting that the Project be accorded a presumption of rolled-in rate

treatment for the purpose of establishing future rates on Natural’s system. In addition,

Natural proposes to use its existing general system fuel retention factors for the Project.

        As set forth in Section IX, Natural has designed its Project to be constructed in a

manner that will minimize impacts to the environment by siting the Project Facilities at its

former compressor station site. The proposed Project Facilities have been designed to

meet the state and federal air emission requirements as well as the Commission’s noise

emission levels.

        As explained in Section X, Public Convenience and Necessity, below, the Project

will provide significant public benefits and is consistent with the Commission’s Statement

of Policy on the Certification of New Interstate Gas Facilities (“Certificate Policy

Statement”).4 As demonstrated herein, the Project is required by the present and future

public convenience and necessity.

                             III.   IDENTITY OF APPLICANT

       The exact legal name of Natural is Natural Gas Pipeline Company of America LLC.

Natural is a limited liability company organized and existing under the laws of the State

of Delaware, with one of its offices located at 3250 Lacey Road, Suite 700, Downers

Grove, Illinois 60515-7918.

              IV.    NATURAL’S EXISTING SYSTEM CONFIGURATION

       Natural’s gas transmission system consists of two mainline systems, the Amarillo

Line and the Gulf Coast Line, as well as the A/G Line connecting the two mainlines. The

Amarillo Line extends from gas producing areas in North Central Texas, Southwest

Texas, Southeast New Mexico, Southwest Oklahoma and the Panhandle areas of Texas

and Oklahoma through the States of New Mexico, Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas, Nebraska,

Iowa and Illinois, terminating at points in and near the Chicago metropolitan area. The

Gulf Coast Line extends from the gas producing areas of South Louisiana and the Gulf

Coast of Texas through the States of Louisiana, Texas, Arkansas, Missouri and Illinois,

terminating at points in and near the Chicago metropolitan area, which are in common

with the terminal points of the Amarillo Line. The Louisiana Line interconnects with the

Gulf Coast Line in Liberty County, Texas and extends eastward into Louisiana in

Vermilion Parish, Louisiana. The A/G Line, an interconnection between the Amarillo Line

and the Gulf Coast Line, runs from Carter County, Oklahoma, to Cass County, Texas.

       Natural is a major transporter of natural gas and provider of natural gas storage

for others. It serves customers along its entire system and also delivers natural gas into

the States of Indiana and Wisconsin. Natural owns and operates substantial underground

storage facilities at locations in the States of Texas, Oklahoma, Iowa and Illinois.

                                     V.      MARKET DEMAND

        Natural’s existing system provides access to numerous supply basins, including

the Haynesville, Permian, and Eagle Ford basins, and markets across its pipeline system

to meet the needs of producers, local distribution companies, marketers, and end use

customers. The Project addresses the need for new pipeline infrastructure to meet the

growing natural gas demand in the Texas Panhandle region for transportation service

along its Amarillo System.

Precedent Agreement, Open Season, and Reserved Capacity

        Pursuant to negotiations between Natural and the Project Shipper, on April 9,

2026, the Project Shipper executed the PA under which Natural has agreed to provide

550,000 Dth/day of firm transportation service under Rate Schedule FTS at a fixed

negotiated rate for a primary term of ten (10) years. The Project Shipper will use this

capacity to supply natural gas to a new natural gas-fired electric generation power plant

to be built in Deaf Smith County, Texas, as part of new data center infrastructure being

built in the Texas Panhandle region. Among other things, the PA required that Natural

conduct a binding open season, in which the Project Shipper’s PA would be considered

a binding bid.

        On July 2, 2026, Natural posted a binding open season notice announcing that it

had entered into a binding transaction with a third party pre-arranged shipper, i.e., the

Project Shipper, and was soliciting additional interest from prospective shippers for firm

transportation associated with the Project (“Open Season”).5 In its Open Season posting,

Natural indicated that the Project could support up to 550,000 Dth/day of firm

        In accordance with Section 5.1(c)(11) of the General Terms and Conditions

Natural has reserved certain receipt point capacity within its Midcontinent Zone.

                       VI.     DESCRIPTION OF PROPOSED FACILITIES

                and station yard piping in Moore County, Texas.

                   VII.    PRECEDENT AGREEMENT AND FTS AGREEMENT

Precedent Agreement

         Natural has executed a binding PA with the Project Shipper that provides the firm

contractual support for the Project. Under the PA, the Project Shipper has elected to pay

a negotiated rate that includes the system-wide option (“SW Option”) under Rate

Schedule FTS,12 with primary receipt points in the Midcontinent Receipt Zone on Natural’s

system, and a primary delivery point to be located in Natural’s Permian Delivery Zone at

Natural’s interconnection with the Project Shipper’s facilities in Deaf Smith County, Texas.

The reservation rate is fixed over the entire term of the firm transportation agreement

(“FTS Agreement”). In addition, the Project Shipper has agreed to a negotiated fuel gas

and gas lost and unaccounted for (“Fuel Gas”) provision with the Fuel Gas percentage

based on a formula. The Project Shipper will also pay the applicable maximum commodity

rate and other applicable surcharges set forth in Natural’s Tariff.

Firm Transportation Agreement

Non-Conforming Creditworthiness Provisions

         Natural is requesting a pre-determination regarding potentially non-conforming

creditworthiness section of the FTS Agreement in Exhibit P, Part II attached to this

application and has redlined the non-conforming provisions for which it seeks a pre-

determination. Although these provisions may be non-conforming, they are permissible

under Commission policy.

         Exhibit D to the FTS Agreement contains provisions addressing credit support and

assurance requirements applicable to the Project Shipper. Specifically, these provisions

require the Project Shipper to provide security in varying amounts necessary to cover the

costs of the Project (which amounts exceed three (3) months of reservation charges) if

the Project Shipper fails to demonstrate creditworthiness in accordance with the

provisions of Natural’s FERC Gas Tariff. The credit assurance amounts are set forth in

Certificate Policy Statement

       The Commission’s Certificate Policy Statement established criteria for determining

whether there is a need for a proposed project and whether the proposed project will

serve the public interest.   In deciding whether to authorize the construction of new

interstate pipeline facilities, the Commission, under the Certificate Policy Statement, will

balance the public benefits created by the proposed project against the potential adverse

consequences that could result from the project. Pursuant to this balancing process, the

                                            22
 Commission has stated that its goal in evaluating new pipeline construction is to give

appropriate consideration to the enhancement of competitive transportation alternatives;

the possibility of overbuilding; subsidization by existing customers; the applicant’s

responsibility for any unsubscribed capacity; the avoidance of unnecessary disruptions of

the environment; and the unneeded exercise of eminent domain.26

        The threshold requirement under the Certificate Policy Statement for a pipeline

proposing a new project is that the applicant must be prepared to financially support the

project without relying on subsidization from existing customers.27          Once the no-

subsidization requirement has been considered, the next inquiry is to determine whether

the applicant has made efforts to eliminate or minimize any adverse effect the project

might have on: 1) applicant’s existing customers, 2) existing pipelines in the market and

their captive customers, or 3) landowners and communities affected by the route of the

new pipeline construction.         If residual adverse effects on these interest groups are

identified after efforts have been made to minimize them, the Commission will evaluate

the project by balancing the evidence of public benefits to be achieved against the

residual adverse effects. The Commission has stated that this is an economic test.28

Only when the benefits outweigh the adverse effects on economic interests will the

Commission proceed to complete the environmental analysis where other interests are

considered.

the test set forth in the Certificate Policy Statement.
